input.quote: (c) ASSIGNMENT. Licensee may not assign this Agreement or assign, sublicense and/or transfer in any manner its license rights hereunder in whole or in part without Licensor's prior written consent.
input.rationale: The assignment clause imposes a blanket bar on Licensee assignment with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard, while placing no restriction at all on Licensor's ability to assign. Worse, Article XX(a) makes any Change of Control of Licensee (including a sale of substantially all assets or a merger) an automatic termination of the Agreement and all of our licences absent Licensor's officer-level consent, with Licensor deemed reasonable in refusing on broad competitive or "interests adversely affected" grounds. That combination is squarely in walk-away territory under this rule and fails the fallback (which at minimum requires mutual successor assignment on notice and a not-unreasonably-withheld standard). The redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out, makes any other assignment subject to consent not unreasonably withheld, restricts Licensor assignment (never to our competitor), and removes the change-of-control termination and consent trigger. Noted but not separately redlined: Article XXII gives Licensor a right of first refusal over our M&A transactions, which we may wish to address under the termination/exit rule.

proposal.summary: Add Customer affiliate/successor assignment carve-out, restrict Licensor assignment, and remove automatic termination on Licensee change of control.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need to be able to assign to an AFFILIATE or to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets without consent, and a change of control of Licensee cannot automatically terminate the Agreement or our licences; our playbook treats a blanket assignment bar plus a change-of-control termination trigger as walk-away. We have also made Licensor's own assignment consent-based (consent not unreasonably withheld, never to our competitor), and are happy to discuss a mutual notice-only successor formulation as a fallback.

ops.newText: Licensee may assign this Agreement and its rights hereunder, in whole or in part, without Licensor's consent to an Affiliate of Licensee or to a successor in connection with a merger, consolidation, reorganization, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or equity. Any other assignment, sublicense or transfer by Licensee requires Licensor's prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld or delayed, and any such attempted assignment without consent will be void and of no effect. Licensor may not assign this Agreement without Licensee's prior written consent (which will not be unreasonably withheld or delayed), and in no event to a competitor of Licensee. A Change of Control of Licensee shall not constitute an assignment requiring consent under this Section

ops.oldText: (a) Upon the occurrence of any Change of Control (as defined below) this Agreement and all Licensee's rights and licenses hereunder shall automatically terminate unless, prior to the occurrence of such Change of Control, Licensor has consented to such Change of Control in a writing executed by an officer of Licensor; provided that Licensor will not unreasonably withhold its consent to the consummation of a Change of Control. For purposes of the preceding sentence, Licensor will be deemed to have reasonably withheld its consent to a Change of Control if any person or entity who would acquire direct or indirect control (as defined below) of Licensee pursuant to such Change of Control then conducts a business that is directly or indirectly competitive with a business then conducted by Licensor or any of its Affiliates and/or Licensor reasonably believes that Licensor's interests will be adversely effected by the continuing of this Agreement upon such a Change in Control.
